candidates.title: Weather challenges search for Vancouver Island man who failed to return from canoe trip
candidates.description: A search is ongoing after James "Dakota" Smith, 34, failed to return from a solo canoe trip off northern Vancouver Island amid stormy weather Friday. Authorities were called to search for Smith after he was a few hours late to return home to his partner and two young children.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Americans in Canada hope midterm results will help mend ties between both countries
candidates.description: Some Americans living in Canada said they were ecstatic at the results of the midterm elections with hopes the two countries will be one step closer to mending economic and cultural relations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Driver dead after tree hits car in Surrey as 2nd windstorm batters B.C.
candidates.description: A driver has died after a fallen tree trapped two vehicles in Surrey on Saturday as a second round of powerful winds battered B.C.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hadden Kelloway once considered leaving Sparwood, B.C. Now he's mayor
candidates.description: Hadden Kelloway once feared he wouldn't be accepted in Sparwood, B.C. Friends and neighbours convinced him to stay. Now, more than 30 years after arriving, he's the town's mayor.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Regina councillor shared great replacement conspiracy theory with colleagues during mosque broadcast debate
candidates.description: Emails obtained by CBC News show internal city discussions about a Regina mosque's decision to broadcast the adhan, or Islamic call to prayer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: York University warns of personal data theft in cybersecurity breach
candidates.description: York University is warning the community of a cybersecurity incident that resulted in the theft of personal information, including personal contact details and student identification numbers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How a one-of-a-kind accessible pool ramp helped a Welland, Ont., woman finally feel safe in the water
candidates.description: A Welland family's journey to have a fully accessible pool installed with a special ramp took years but was finally completed.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is the Alberta government engaging in American-style gerrymandering?
candidates.description: Political science experts told CBC’s West of Centre that Alberta’s electoral map-making process should be reexamined to stave off American influences.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: An Ontario nature sanctuary home to over 70 rare species will now be protected for generations to come
candidates.description: A nature sanctuary in Whitby, Ont., home to over 70 rare species, some of which are at-risk, is now part of the Ontario Nature reserve system after its acquisition of the forested area from its previous land trust owners last week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Birds of a feather: Human speech and birdsong have a lot in common, McGill study finds
candidates.description: Researchers from McGill University have found many of the same vocal patterns that appear in bird species — including small pitch intervals and phrase elongation — are also present in human song and speech.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Regional gaps in safe sport rules remain a 'major' concern for Canada's sport integrity agency
candidates.description: More than six months on from a report that rang alarm bells about the prevalence of abuse and maltreatment in sport, the head of Canada’s sport integrity agency continues to have “major” concerns about regional gaps in safe sport rules.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Absolutely' possible: Vancouver, Victoria mayors back Ottawa's bid to end homelessness
candidates.description: The federal Liberal budget, delivered on Thursday, has set aside $11.2 billion over the next four years in a bid to end homelessness in the next 10 years.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kahnawà:ke honours veterans at annual Remembrance Day parade
candidates.description: Veterans, military members and community residents gathered in Kahnawà:ke for the annual Remembrance Day parade, honouring those who served in the Canadian and U.S. armed forces. The event, organized in collaboration with the Mohawk Legion, brought generations together to remember veterans, recognize the community’s long history of military service and celebrate a legacy they hope will continue.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Northern, remote RCMP detachments chronically and critically understaffed: internal report
candidates.description: Northern and isolated RCMP detachments have become "chronically and at times critically" understaffed, according to an internal evaluation report — the latest document pointing to retention and recruitment issues within the storied organization.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Outages expected, more ferries cancelled amid wind warnings for B.C.'s South Coast
candidates.description: After a round of blustery fall weather caused ferry cancellations and knocked out power to thousands, B.C. appears set for another blast of wind.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: He quit firefighting for his mental health. Then he came to the rescue after a horrific bus crash
candidates.description: A lonely highway, a traumatized son, and up to 20 people in need of urgent care after a horrific bus crash: that's the situation Rich Rogers found himself in Wednesday morning along Highway 39, just south of Mackenzie, B.C. A former firefighter, he spoke to reporters about the toll it can take and the importance of supporting first responders.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As Europe prepares for the worst, Britons get schooled in preparedness
candidates.description: With fears of cyberattacks, conflict and major disruption to daily life grow in Europe, governments are urging citizens to prepare for emergencies. But in Britain, the culture of stockpiling supplies and being ready to face a crisis needs gentle and convincing persuasion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 7 killed, more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
candidates.description: The crash occurred in the al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 52 kilometers south of Cairo. A train travelling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poland in mourning after deadly mass shooting in Krakow
candidates.description: Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, after authorities say a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow and opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15 others before police shot and wounded him.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Norway says it has been bumped by the IIHF to allow Russia to compete at world juniors in Canada
candidates.description: The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said Sunday it has been informed that it is being bumped by Russia from competing in the world junior championships in Canada, a decision creating further uncertainty involving the 10-nation tournament.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Republicans took big hits in the U.S. midterms. Does that mean Trump's political era is over?
candidates.description: As the dust settles on a stunning midterm election that saw Republicans take heavy losses in the U.S. Congress, former Canadian and American officials are unsure if the drubbing signals the end of U.S. President Donald Trump's political era and movement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How the Democrats' midterm wave shows a path back to the presidency
candidates.description: Democrats remain cautious about jumping to conclusions of what their midterm wins could mean for the next presidential election campaign. Still, the dramatic scale of the victory has some seeing a potential path back to the White House in 2028.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What needs to happen for Canada to join Europe's flagship student exchange program?
candidates.description: Canada is negotiating to be a part of a major European exchange program that could give Canadians more opportunities to study, work and live in Europe. But how Canada would expand its participation in Erasmus+ is complicated.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israel's president asks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's rival, to form new government
candidates.description: Israel's president has tapped opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, in another setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UFC boss Dana White says he's meeting with Trump after press secretary job offer
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Paraguay's impeached ex-president charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
candidates.description: Paraguayan prosecutors on Saturday charged former president Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain and asked a court to jail him pending trial, a day after his ​impeachment over the collapse of digital lender Ueno.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The age of AI warfare has dawned. Is Canada ready?
candidates.description: Countries like the U.S., U.K. and China are pouring billions into AI-integrated military software and hardware, despite legal and ethical concerns. Canadian defence technology companies, military experts and defence officials all say keeping humans in the loop will be key.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Europeans protest construction of large AI data centres across continent
candidates.description: Demonstrators are calling for a moratorium on constructing large AI data centres across Europe. Data centres are a lightning rod for concerns and criticisms over artificial intelligence due to their role in developing and operating the technology, which involves using massive amounts of electricity and water.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's military is using Palantir software. What are the risks?
candidates.description: Canada has multimillion-dollar contracts with U.S. tech firm Palantir. Experts warn the deals could expose military data to U.S. authorities and deepen Canada's reliance on foreign technology, while DND says its systems keep government data secure in Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why the U.S. midterm results may show 'money stops mattering'
candidates.description: Republicans had a significant edge over Democrats in raising funding from outside groups in this year's U.S. midterms, giving them an overall money advantage. Yet Republicans suffered significant losses, raising questions about the impact money has in a political race.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornell faculty vote no confidence in university's leadership
candidates.description: The faculty senate of Cornell University approved a resolution Friday declaring no confidence in the school's top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecting deep discontent on campus in the wake of a former student's lawsuit saying she was gang raped at a fraternity party in 2024.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. sanctions Canadian money-exchange businesses allegedly connected to Iranian regime, Ryan Wedding
candidates.description: The United States government has announced sanctions against several Canadian currency-exchange businesses accused of helping the Iranian regime and, in several cases, also helping the alleged head of a drug trafficking ring.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ousted Paraguayan president placed under house arrest
candidates.description: Ousted Paraguayan president Santiago Peña was placed under house arrest Friday on suspicion of breach of trust and influence peddling, among other charges, shortly after the Senate removed him from office over the collapse of a government-linked bank that locked nearly half of the country's six million people out of their savings.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What Ottawa's 'RRSP for life' plan means for Canadian seniors
candidates.description: The federal budget proposes a tweak to Registered Retirement Savings Plans (RRSPs) aimed at simplifying financial planning for thousands of seniors every year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How Trump's tariffs are threatening to spoil the success of Canadian cheese
candidates.description: In recent years, Canadian cheese has been having a bit of a moment south of the border, taking home some of the biggest awards in the Western hemisphere. But Trump's 50 per cent tariffs on certain dairy products, including Canadian cheese, are threatening to spoil this success.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poilievre pans Liberal budget's $15M capital gains exemption, calls for 'simpler' plan
candidates.description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is criticizing a key feature of the Carney government's latest budget, arguing the proposed $15-million capital gains exemption on the sale of qualifying shares from a Canadian company applies too narrowly, excluding key businesses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
candidates.description: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
candidates.description: The national mood is low, and faith in politics even lower - with voters deserting the major parties at the polls.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
candidates.description: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks
candidates.description: The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
candidates.description: The 82-year-old appeared in court in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
candidates.description: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Texas mayor instructs police to limit co-operation with ICE
candidates.description: There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
candidates.description: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
candidates.description: It is yet unclear what caused the accident but Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation is underway and will "hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
candidates.description: While some believe the site should be partially or completely rebuilt, others want it abandoned and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed
candidates.description: Jehovah's Witness leaders relaxed strict rules on blood transfusions, but the change came 23 days too late for Isaac Valdez.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
candidates.description: The US president's promotion of Miller, a loyal partisan firebrand to be his new chief of staff sets up likely clashes with Congress.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
candidates.description: For some tourists, the contrast between Somalia's reputation and what they experience on the ground can be striking.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
candidates.description: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?
candidates.description: Nintendo has released its remake of what is considered one of the best games ever made - the BBC's Tom Gerken gives his verdict.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
candidates.description: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: One of the year's most prolific meteor showers to light up the night sky this weekend
candidates.description: The Leonid meteor shower, known for its bright and fast meteors, will kick off this weekend and continue until the end of November.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
candidates.description: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
candidates.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
candidates.description: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
candidates.description: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
candidates.description: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel's president taps opposition candidate, not Netanyahu, to form a government
candidates.description: Gadi Eisenkot ran as the main rival to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but neither won enough support to command a majority. Israel's main parties have recommended Eisenkot form a new government.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
candidates.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
candidates.description: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The Cybertruck's 'cause of death?' Insufficient demand
candidates.description: One of the most polarizing vehicles to hit the road will soon be a thing of history. Tesla will wind down manufacturing of its Cybertruck at the company's Gigafactory Texas mid-next year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This was the week the AI trade cracked. So what's next?
candidates.description: Big losses by AI shares in stock markets after Democrats won the midterm elections have left investors shaken and wondering comes next.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
candidates.description: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A promising new medicine against heart disease fails unexpectedly
candidates.description: Doctors expected an experimental drug that lowers a common risk factor for heart attacks would save patients' lives. The medicine made no difference.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: This teen boy set out to get people talking about periods. He's now a Diana honoree
candidates.description: This year's the Princess Diana honor roll highlights 198 inspiring young activists and advocates — including an 18-year-old guy in India who founded Team Period.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: * WHAT...Isolated minor coastal flooding. * WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County, Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County. * WHEN...Through Monday morning. * IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property.

candidates.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. candidates.description: At 413 PM AST, emergency management reported that PR - 31 km 8.0 remains closed due flooding waters. The latest USGS river gauge at Rio Blanco in Naguabo reported 11.39 ft, reaching moderate flooding stage. Between 2 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Emergency management reported. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. This includes the following streams and drainages... Rio Espiritu Santo, Bahia Algodones to Ensenada Honda Coastal Watersheds, Rio Gurabo, Rio Juan Martin, Rio Sabana at mouth, Rio Santiago, Rio Pitahaya, Rio Blanco, Rio Cubuy, Coastal Watershed, Rio Fajardo, Rio Espiritu Santo near mouth, Rio Icacos, Quebrada Fajardo to Laguna Grande Coastal Drainage Watersheds, Rio Anton Ruiz and Rio Mameyes.
